$schema_note: Companion database to CONTENT-SOURCING-GUIDELINES.md. Each entry is referenced by ID from a module's provenance.sources array. Seed list — verify URLs and expand per-domain before relying on it at scale. 'domains' uses the same dag_branch-style codes as arc-module_schema.json.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 — Guide for Conducting Risk Assessments
sources.notes: Primary reference for risk lifecycle / threat-vulnerability-risk-treatment content.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations
sources.notes: Control families reference — technical / administrative / physical control classification.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2 — Computer Security Incident Handling Guide
NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
sources.notes: Govern/Identify/Protect/Detect/Respond/Recover functions — useful structural backbone, don't mirror its own section headers verbatim.

sources.title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0
sources.notes: Core AI risk framework, published Jan 2023. Also tracked on the AEGIS roadmap for Domain 6 content.

sources.title: NIST AI 600-1 — Generative AI Profile
sources.notes: 12-risk GenAI companion profile to the AI RMF, published Jul 2024.

sources.title: CISA Cybersecurity Advisories & Best Practices
sources.publisher: CISA (US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency)
sources.notes: Use for current threat advisories and operational guidance; content changes frequently, re-verify per module.

sources.title: OWASP Top 10:2021
sources.notes: Attribute OWASP by name when referenced. Paraphrase vulnerability descriptions — do not reuse their category text verbatim.

sources.title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM & GenAI Applications
sources.notes: Roadmap notes a 2026 edition superseding 2025 v2.0, published Aug 4, 2026 — confirm current edition at time of authoring, this project moves fast.

sources.title: MITRE ATT&CK
sources.license: Free to use with attribution under MITRE's ATT&CK terms of use
sources.notes: Tactics/techniques taxonomy — good structural reference for SOC/incident-response content. Cite technique IDs (e.g. T1566) rather than reproducing MITRE's descriptions.

sources.title: MITRE ATLAS (Adversarial Threat Landscape for AI Systems)
sources.license: Free to use with attribution under MITRE's terms
sources.notes: AI/ML-specific adversarial tactics matrix. Confirm matrix version at build per roadmap note.

sources.title: RFC 2196 — Site Security Handbook
sources.license: Freely available; IETF reproduction terms apply — paraphrase, don't republish RFC text
sources.notes: Foundational, somewhat dated (1997) — good for concepts (AUPs, security policy structure), not for current technical specifics.

sources.title: CIS Critical Security Controls v8
sources.license: Free to use with attribution; CIS license has non-commercial conditions — check current terms before use
sources.notes: 18-control structure, useful as a secondary triangulation source alongside NIST SP 800-53.

sources.title: AWS Security Documentation (IAM, Well-Architected Security Pillar)
sources.license: Copyrighted vendor documentation — cite as source, never reproduce
sources.notes: Use for real-world cloud IAM/network examples; always paraphrase and build original worked examples.

sources.title: Microsoft Learn — Azure Security Documentation
sources.license: Copyrighted vendor documentation — cite as source, never reproduce
sources.notes: Same usage rule as AWS entry above.

restricted_do_not_source.reason: Copyrighted CBK, courseware, and exam outline text. Domain alignment (naming which CC domain a module maps to) is fine — sourcing content from ISC2 text is not.
Copyrighted exam objectives documents and courseware. Same domain-alignment vs. content-sourcing distinction as ISC2.
Paywalled standards documents (e.g. 27001, 27002) — not open, regardless of citation frequency elsewhere. Reference their existence/purpose only.
Copyright risk plus certification-revocation risk for learners who studied from the same leaked material CompTIA screens for.

restricted_do_not_source.publisher: Other paid prep providers (Udemy courses, Boson, etc.)
restricted_do_not_source.reason: Their expression of a concept is their own copyrighted work, same reasoning as ISC2/CompTIA.
